_note: What each case study shows. Every excerpt is copied verbatim from the project's own repository (file and line numbers given); terminal output is a real recorded run. Pictures are the project's own screenshots. 'also' lists extra figures shown only on the case study page.

tributary.alt: Tributary's file view in dark mode, with an upload panel showing three files streaming to Drive at 31%, 20% and 44%.
tributary.caption: Tributary's web app while three resumable uploads stream to a linked Drive account. From the demo on tributary.swayam.li.

also.alt: Screen recording of Tributary's web app: browsing files, uploading and moving them between linked Drive accounts.
also.caption: A 28-second recording of the web app, from tributary.swayam.li.
One origin: a Node server serves the React app and proxies the API. The Go server keeps its records and background jobs in PostgreSQL, and reaches every Drive account through one provider interface.

plugfit.caption: How a spec becomes a live endpoint: the API takes the spec, a Celery job cleans it with Gemini 2.0 Flash, and the executor registry serves the result over a custom MCP transport, isolated per tenant.

sandboxd.caption: What happens to one request: Sandboxd checks it, looks the language up in its registry, then compiles and runs the code inside NsJail, every test case in its own sandboxed process, and returns a verdict for each.

also.caption: An example request from the API docs: a C program and one test case.
The response the docs show for it: the build, then each test with its output, time and memory.

dnsr.caption: How dnsr resolved www.github.com in one real run: it starts at a root server and follows each referral down. Every server is asked for only one more label than its own zone, so the root never sees the full name.

also.title: dnsr www.github.com
also.code:
$ dnsr www.github.com
;; resolving www.github.com. A
→ asking e.root-servers.net. (192.203.230.10) for com. NS
↓ e.root-servers.net. → referral to com. [a.gtld-servers.net, b.gtld-servers.net, c.gtld-servers.net, +10 more] (84ms)
→ asking j.gtld-servers.net. (192.48.79.30) for github.com. NS
↓ j.gtld-servers.net. → referral to github.com. [ns-520.awsdns-01.net, ns-421.awsdns-52.com, ns-1707.awsdns-21.co.uk, +5 more] (169ms)
→ asking ns-421.awsdns-52.com. (205.251.193.165) for www.github.com. A
↪ CNAME www.github.com. is an alias → github.com., restarting from the top
  │ ↷ starting at cached zone github.com.
  │ → asking ns-421.awsdns-52.com. (205.251.193.165) for github.com. A
  │ ✓ ns-421.awsdns-52.com. answered 1 A record(s) (76ms)

;; NOERROR · 4 hops · 388ms
www.github.com.                3600 IN CNAME github.com.
github.com.                      60 IN A     20.207.73.82
also.caption: The same run as dnsr prints it, from the README.

vulnscan.caption: What a scan does: VulnScan finds the dependency files, asks OSV.dev about every package in batches (cached on disk), scores each advisory with its own CVSS v3.1 calculator, and writes a report and a fix script for you to review.

also.caption: The end of that CVSS v3.1 calculator, written from the FIRST.org formula.

boids-sim.alt: The original Boids Simulation: a hundred pink dots flocking on a cream canvas, running in the browser as WebAssembly.
boids-sim.caption: The original, in Go with Ebiten, compiled to WebAssembly. The flock at the top of this page uses its rules.

6502-emulator.alt: The 6502 playground: an assembly program that prints a string, beside the console, registers, status flags and a memory view.
6502-emulator.caption: The emulator compiled to WebAssembly, with an assembler, console, registers and memory view.

grain.alt: Grain’s sandbox: a pile of sand on a wooden plank above a stone tank of water.
grain.caption: The starting scene in Grain. Try fire on the plank or acid on the sand pile.

thompson.alt: Thompson’s visualizer: the pattern (a|b)*abb and the string babaabb, the NFA with its active states lit, and the tape of characters being read.
thompson.caption: The NFA for (a|b)*abb reading babaabb. Every lit state is one the machine is in; the tape below shows the string being read.
